correctness.rationale: With p=K/N and q=1−p the two hypergeometric masses are p at K−1 and q at K, and both binomial masses are C(N,K)p^Kq^(N−K). This gives (N−1)H(p)−log C(N,K) in nats. The all-composition Stirling error O(1/K+1/(N−K)) is uniformly bounded; if pq tends to zero along a maximizing subsequence, its log-pq term tends to minus infinity relative to the center, a contradiction. Uniform interior Stirling and the strict maximum of F at u=p−1/2=0 then give u→0. Expanding half log(pq)−H in 2u cancels the quadratic term and gives −(8/3)u^4+O(u^6) relative to the center, with all higher even coefficients negative. The Stirling coefficient has increment (4/3)u^2/(1−4u^2). Comparing to the nearest central point, whose baseline error is O(N^-3), gives (8/3)u^4≤C u^2/N+O(N^-3), hence y=√N u is bounded for all maximizers. On bounded y the rescaled profile is uniformly (4/3)y^2−(8/3)y^4+o(1); compare with lattice approximations to ±1/2, possible even for odd N. Every maximizing subsequence approaches that two-point set and the limiting gain is 1/6. The baseline constants F(0)=−2 log 2 and G(0)=1/4 give exactly the absolute expansion including the coefficient 1/(6N²).
residual_risks: No uploaded code was run and the finite checks were not independently rerun; they are illustrative only. The proof gives an asymptotic for every maximizing choice, not an exact finite-N maximizer formula.

evidence: Johnson–Gavalakis–Kontoyiannis treat relative entropy with composition dependence, but their compared bounds use samples of size at most half of the population. Harremoës–Matúš's Theorem 5.1 gives a limiting expression in the limiting unsampled fraction, for fixed color count and proportions away from zero. It gives no composition-dependent expansion as this fraction goes to zero; interpreting its limit at zero as divergent still gives no optimizing composition or correction.
Dümbgen–Samworth–Wellner compare hypergeometric and binomial laws via maximal density ratios, not the same divergence, and the inspected bound has a sample-size restriction.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither other sampling regimes nor bounds on a different discrepancy give the endpoint quartic/quadratic competition. The decisive coverage is the exact endpoint treatment in the catalogue.

evidence: The uniform Stirling formula in the covering record uses G(p)=log(p(1−p))/2−h(p) and A(p)=(1/p+1/(1−p)−1)/12. It gives an O(n^-3) remainder. At p=floor(n/2)/n, p−1/2=O(n^-1); the same proof gives a quartic G increment and quadratic A increment.
Thus D_n(floor(n/2))=log(πn/8)/2+1/(4n)+O(n^-3), since G(1/2)=−2 log 2 and A(1/2)=1/4.
